title: lucille.exec/1 files.search document
description: What files.search returns, JSON-encoded in the stdout of its reply: the matches ripgrep found, each with its path relative to the folder, its line number and its line, as ripgrep's --json gives them. The reply's stdout_truncated is the document's truncated; an empty stdout, with the flag true, is a request cap too small for any document. Two closed shapes: the matches found, with error null, or ripgrep's output unread, with no matches, truncated true and error unreadable_output. The byte bounds on paths and lines are the host's (rule search-bytes); the schema bounds characters.

matches.description: In the order ripgrep wrote them: by path, then by line.

truncated.description: True when not every match ripgrep wrote, or would have written, is here: past 1000 matches, past the stream's cap, a path over 4096 bytes, output the host did not keep or a search that did not end on its own, or a private-key block that did not end.

document.unreadable.description: ripgrep wrote a line the host does not read as one of its messages, and nothing of its output is here.

path.description: The file's path relative to the folder searched, never absolute and with no .. part.

lines.description: The matching line, with the line ending it had, cut at 1000 bytes.

line_truncated.description: True when the line was longer than 1000 bytes and is cut.

path_text.description: A path that is valid UTF-8 and holds no U+0000: relative, its parts joined by /, none of them empty or .., so never absolute. At most 4096 characters here, and at most 4096 bytes of UTF-8 by rule search-bytes.

path_bytes.description: A path that is not valid UTF-8: its bytes in standard base64 with padding. At most 5464 characters here, and at most 4096 bytes by rule search-bytes.

line_text.description: A line that is valid UTF-8 and holds no U+0000. At most 1000 characters here, and at most 1000 bytes of UTF-8 by rule search-bytes.

line_bytes.description: A line that is not valid UTF-8, or holds NUL: its bytes in standard base64 with padding. At most 1336 characters here, and at most 1000 bytes by rule search-bytes.
